nodes.prompt:
TASK: Dispatch exactly one retained ChatGPT Web helper batch containing the two implementation tasks below.
DELIVERABLE: Return the complete helper JSON result for every worker, including scope_id, browser binding, terminal state, completion_check, workspace_revision, and any authoritative error.
SCOPE: Read only /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite/ORCA_LITE_FIX_PLAN.md and repository state to assemble the two supplied task objects. Do not edit repository files yourself. Invoke only /Users/indo/code/project/omo-bridge/target/debug/delegate_to_chatgpt_web once, with --batch-stdin --json; leave --browser-driver unset so cmux discovery falls back to Orca. Do not create a second helper, close any scope, use --close-on-terminal, or bypass capacity/rate-limit controls.
VERIFY: The helper process exits 0, returns two distinct scope_id values, and each terminal worker reports ready=true through its completion evidence. If it instead returns an authoritative terminal error, capacity exhaustion, or rate-limit cooldown, report that exact JSON without retrying.
STOP WHEN: Report the helper JSON result or its authoritative terminal error.

The JSON batch sent to the helper MUST contain these exact independent tasks, each with workspace /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite:

1. label: orca-lite-backend-phase-3-8
TASK: Finish all remaining backend portions of ORCA_LITE_FIX_PLAN.md and commit the requested verified increments.
DELIVERABLE: Backend-only source/test/config edits, two atomic commits when the seams are independently green (the existing writer-lease completion first, then remaining backend safety/IPC/performance work), and a report of exact commit hashes plus test/clippy output.
SCOPE: You may read the whole repository and write only src-tauri/**. You may read but MUST NOT edit ui/**, ORCA_LITE_FIX_PLAN.md, .omo/**, or root package files. Preserve unrelated working-tree changes. Start by inspecting the existing uncommitted writer-lease work in src-tauri/src/worktree/{manager,model,git}.rs, src-tauri/src/ipc/worktree.rs, and src-tauri/tests/worktree_safety.rs; complete its terminal lifecycle integration and its regression evidence before committing it. Then implement the remaining backend plan phases: WorkspaceRegistry with canonical allowed-root and symlink/leading-dash protection; resolve terminal and worktree IPC by registered workspace/worktree identity instead of untrusted paths or raw shell command strings; stable structured IPC error DTOs; CSP activation in src-tauri/tauri.conf.json and minimum Tauri capability adjustment if needed; worktree_changed events for successful mutations; explicit camelCase serde DTOs; and move synchronous Git command work out of async Tauri command execution using spawn_blocking while preserving error behavior. Retain default safe branch deletion and explicit destructive path. Add behavioral regression tests for every changed security or lifecycle seam. Do not use raw string parsing for error branching. Do not use destructive git commands.
VERIFY: First run each new regression test red for the intended missing behavior, then run cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml and cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings; both must exit 0 before reporting. Confirm git diff is limited to allowed files, and report file paths and commit hashes.
STOP WHEN: The two backend commits exist with all backend acceptance commands exiting 0, or one concrete unresolvable failure is reported with its command output.

2. label: orca-lite-frontend-phase-7-8
TASK: Finish all remaining frontend portions of ORCA_LITE_FIX_PLAN.md and commit the requested verified increments.
DELIVERABLE: Frontend-only source/tests/performance-note edits, an atomic commit for the existing IPC wrapper/camelCase/error-code completion and a separate commit for bundle/lifecycle optimization when independently green, with exact commit hashes and test/build evidence.
SCOPE: You may read the whole repository and write only ui/** plus a new root PERF_NOTES.md. You may read but MUST NOT edit src-tauri/**, ORCA_LITE_FIX_PLAN.md, .omo/**, or other root files. Preserve unrelated working-tree changes. Begin with the uncommitted App.tsx, deleted ui/src/types.ts, ui/src/lib/tauri.test.ts, and ui/src/lib/ipcErrors.test.ts. Finish a single typed Tauri wrapper surface, no component-level direct command strings, camelCase contract types, and structured-code error branching. Then lazy-load xterm and WebGL renderer assets without changing terminal session ownership, retain Canvas fallback/context-loss cleanup, instrument observable WebGL lifecycle resource counts, and record measured build/lifecycle evidence in PERF_NOTES.md. Add behavior-focused tests only; do not pin prose.
VERIFY: First execute each added regression test in its intended red state, then run bun --cwd ui test and bun --cwd ui run build with exit code 0. Confirm build artifact chunk sizing and lifecycle instrumentation values are documented. Confirm git diff is limited to allowed files plus PERF_NOTES.md, and report commit hashes.
STOP WHEN: The frontend commits exist with test and build commands exiting 0, or one concrete unresolvable failure is reported with its command output.

nodes.prompt:
TASK: Run the complete repository acceptance checks after the retained Web implementation batch reaches its terminal state.
DELIVERABLE: A PASS/FAIL report containing each literal command, exit code, and relevant final output, plus git status --short.
SCOPE: Read the whole /Users/indo/code/project/orca-lite repository and test/build outputs only. Do not edit files, create or close Web sessions, make commits, or use destructive Git commands.
VERIFY: Run exactly: cargo test --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml; cargo clippy --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings; bun --cwd ui test; bun --cwd ui run build. PASS requires all four commands to exit 0. Then inspect the built UI artifact using the real production build output and report chunk-size warnings or their absence.
STOP WHEN: Report PASS with captured evidence for all four exit-0 commands, or FAIL with the first concrete command failure and output.
